items.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025
items.q: The interviewer mentions Charlie Rouse in the context of Thelonious Monk; the interviewee does not mention Rouse or indicate a personal connection.

ctx.x: Yup. Um hum. Yup. I had a few of those classes, and every semester when I was teaching in Boston I always bring in music. You know we learn how to plan everything but I’ll say okay we’ve got to listen to some music. So I’d sit them all down, I’d put on a recording of Monk — Thelonious Monk — and I’d tell the kids, “Okay, when this music comes on do whatever you want to do, just don’t hurt anybody.” And nine times out of ten they all danced to Monk. And so I was like okay, this is what the music does for people…

That’s a heck of a coincidence because last night on the way home they were playing Thelonious Monk on the Sirius jazz station and it was so — he was really into hitting these chords where no one else would do it and, you know, Charlie Rouse was, I mean the whole thing was very physical. And so I can almost picture that class you are talking about.
